text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu intervened to prevent Palestinian Waqf from expelling Jordanians from al-Aqsa complex.
- Netanyahu approved oil drilling in Golan.
- Committee recommends closing Bar Ilan street during prayers.
- Airport workers on strike at Ben Gurion today.
- News Datacom president: The information that prompted the investigation against us came from vengeful people.
JERUSALEM POST
- State Rabin memorial held at Mt. Herzl: "A year has passed; nothing has changed".
- "Constructive ambiguity" may help solve hot pursuit impasse.
- Betar, Bnei Akiva refuse to sing "A Song of Peace".
- Soldiers, settlers warned of possible kidnappings.
- Deadline passes with no change in PLO Covenant.
- Jordanian diplomat: Syrians planning surprise attack.
- Safra to buy UMB Trust for $30 million.
- French dairy to buy 20% of Strauss Dairies.
MAARIV
- Progress in talks on Hebron amidst concern over possible guerrilla attack.
- Syria: The U.S. twisted our messages of reassurance to Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu and Arafat expected to meet at beginning of next week.
- Deep recession expected in 1997.
- Poll: 57% think Hebron redeployment will lead to bloodshed.
GLOBES
- Safra brothers bought Bank Mizrahi in New York for $30 million.
- Assessment: I.D.B. will appoint its own head of Clal in place of Olshanski.
